text:
mira: RFC follow-up: picking a long-term direction for the continuous-batcher scheduler. We prototyped 3 variants; need to choose one to stabilize. Short names: soft-reserve, strict-isolation, and hybrid-ledger.

eli: quick ask: what are the user-visible SLO impacts? p99, cold-starts, and cost per token are the primary concerns.

mira: soft-reserve = best steady-state packing, lower cost for random small-request workloads, but higher susceptibility to noisy tenant spikes -> p99 jitter. strict-isolation = predictable p99, higher idle waste, easier SLO guarantees. hybrid-ledger = like soft-reserve but with a ledger that charges excess tokens and forces migration when credit drains.

sam: ledger sounds clever but operationally heavy. Do we have a simple guard against runaway tenants for soft-reserve?

mira: yeah: token headroom with TTL, adaptive backpressure signals, and automatic fast-fail to strict lanes if a tenant breaches sustained-rate thresholds. We also add a per-tenant cooldown to avoid thrash.

jordan: SDK/API constraints: I want admission to remain small: enqueue(req), hint({deadline, tokens}), cancel(id). No lane leak to callers. Internals decide lane mapping.

anu: agree. also propose a tiny-request fastpath: if tokens <= 12 and no prefetch hint, route to microbatch fastpath which bypasses prefetch and avoids kv-cache churn. We saw a 30% tail reduction in bench.

eli: about heartbeats: are we relying on runtime heartbeats for headroom, or do we keep counters in the allocator and reconcile? Heartbeat adds control-plane work but is simpler for eviction reasoning.

mira: leaning heartbeat + aggregator service. We can compress and sample heartbeats (every 100ms default, adaptive up to 500ms under load).

sam: +1 for heartbeat. Also need an admin pin to force strict lanes during incidents.

jordan: observability needs: per-lane p50/p95/p99, microbatch size distribution, preempt count, preempt latency tax, and tenant kv-cache hit rates. Those metrics must flow to the Console.

mira: rollout plan sketch: canary on 2 hosts with soft-reserve enabled, fallback window=200ms, heartbeat interval=100ms, cooldown= max(1s, 3x tenant p95). If noisy tenant detected, auto-migrate with a 10s quiet period.

infra-bot: deploy-check ok for canary: 2 nodes, telemetry hooks enabled.

anu: eviction hysteresis note: when moving tenants to strict lanes, keep a 30s grace before allowing another migration back. avoids oscillation on load spikes.

mira: noted. I'll author the follow-up doc with config knobs and a compatibility shim: enqueue calls without hint default to conservative deadline inference.

eli: i'll prototype a compressed pb for heartbeats and an aggregator sketch. We'll also add a test that fuzzes heartbeat loss and ensures bounded p99.

mira: thanks all. I'll post the design draft this afternoon. :thumbsup:
